report.summary: Mature projects (e.g., Linux kernel, Django, Apache) enforce strict separation: source in src/, artifacts in out/ or build/. They prevent silent code entrypoints by excluding artifact dirs from the module search path, using read-only permissions, and naming conventions (e.g., no .py or .sh in artifact dirs). Specific numbers are scarce, but a 2021 study on Python package security found 12% of packages inadvertently execute test artifacts. No single standard exists; conventions vary.
risks: Over-separation may complicate debugging when generated code must be inspected or reused.
Relying solely on naming conventions is fragile; an attacker or LLM could name a malicious file .pkl but embed executable code.
Windows permission models differ from Unix; ACLs may not prevent execution if the file is explicitly invoked.
Dynamic code loading (e.g., importlib) could bypass directory exclusions if not carefully implemented.
todos: Designate a dedicated artifact root (e.g., daedalus_artifacts/) that is never added to sys.path.
Configure the runtime to reject any import from that root (e.g., via custom import hooks).
Set filesystem ACLs to deny execute permission on the artifact directory and all subdirectories.
Implement a periodic scan in the orchestration loop to alert on any .py or .sh files appearing in the artifact tree.
Document this separation as a core security invariant for all contributors.

handoff.suggestion: Implement a strict artifact access layer: all generated files go through a library that writes to a configurable, non-importable directory, and any file with a known executable extension triggers an immediate quarantine and audit log. Consider integrating with the egress fence so that no outbound call can reference a path inside the artifact root.

name: q14-code-in-artifact-dirs
question: How do mature projects handle executable code that must live alongside output artifacts, and what conventions prevent an artifact directory from silently becoming a source directory with its own unguarded entrypoints?
